organization.description: Stratum Graphene Technologies manufactures large-area monolayer graphene via roll-to-roll chemical vapor deposition (CVD), performs scalable transfer and lamination into aerospace-qualified epoxy systems, and operates an accredited mechanical testing laboratory focused on composite fatigue, interlaminar shear, and compression-after-impact relevant to primary and secondary aerostructures. The company emphasizes empirical datasets—static strength, fatigue life, environmental aging—not unsubstantiated theoretical claims about graphene performance.

technical_poc.name: Dr. Samuel Okonkwo
technical_poc.title: Chief Technology Officer
technical_poc.background_summary: Materials scientist with 16 years in aerospace composites manufacturing and qualification (AS9100 environments). Led teams qualifying carbon/epoxy prepreg structures for UAV primary structures and introduced graphene-enhanced interleaf concepts with statistically powered fatigue datasets (stress-life curves, environmental conditioning per ASTM). Expertise in scalable lamination, void management, and standardized coupon-to-element validation pathways suitable for white paper responses grounded in test evidence.

administrative_poc.name: Kevin Porter
administrative_poc.title: Contracts Manager
administrative_poc.responsibilities: Handles proprietary marking, submission packaging for RFIs, NDAs with aerospace primes, and coordination for controlled facility tours under visitor protocols.

focus_areas: Roll-to-roll monolayer graphene synthesis and defect mapping
Transfer & lamination into aerospace epoxy systems (controlled void content)
Structural composites testing: tension/compression, ILSS, CAI, fatigue
Hybrid laminates: graphene interlayers vs baseline carbon fiber/epoxy
Manufacturing cost modeling ($/lb Part + scrap + recurring NRE amortization)
research_profile.research_description: Stratum's operating model pairs scalable graphene sheet supply with statistically framed structural validation. For aerospace load-bearing applications, the company emphasizes through-thickness integrity (interlaminar toughening hypothesis tested via Mode I/II fracture surrogates), not cosmetic conductivity enhancements. Stratum maintains traceable lab datasets comparing baseline UD carbon/epoxy coupons against graphene-interleaved architectures under identical cure cycles and fiber areal weights.
research_profile.prior_experience: Delivered pilot-line graphene interlayers for a regional UAV OEM demonstrator wing spar cap (non-flight article); joint testing campaign with a Tier 1 aerostructures supplier comparing fatigue crack growth trends vs baseline laminate under matched spectrum loading.

prior_publications.title: Fatigue Performance of Graphene-Interleaved Carbon/Epoxy Laminates Under Spectrum Loading
prior_publications.relevance_to_proposal: Provides substantiating fatigue data aligned with RFI emphasis on static/fatigue substantiation.

prior_publications.relevance_to_proposal: Addresses out-of-plane and interlaminar strength themes requested by DARPA-SN-26-62.

prior_publications.relevance_to_proposal: Supports joining/scaling discussion relevant to building larger structural constructs from sheets.

breakdown.notes: Absorbed as bid & proposal / IRAD allocation; not reimbursed per RFI disclaimers.

project_goals.primary_objective: Provide DARPA/TTO with empirical, manufacturing-grounded insight into graphene sheet scalability, joining strategies, structural substantiation datasets, and realistic weight/cost trades for aerospace load-bearing structures—explicitly excluding theoretical assertions without data and excluding non-structural sensor integrations unless tied to load-bearing applications.

technical_goals.title: Document largest manufacturable graphene sheet dimensions & grading methodology
technical_goals.description: Report roll-width/continuous length limits for monolayer graphene sheets suitable for structural lamination, including thickness uniformity definitions and defect thresholds tied to mechanical bins.
technical_goals.success_metric: Clear dimensional envelope + QC correlation to lap-shear / ILSS surrogate metrics.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: White paper Section + summary tables (within 5-page constraint).

technical_goals.title: Outline scalable joining pathways for larger aerostructure blanks
technical_goals.description: Describe overlap/scarf strategies for graphene-bearing prepreg stacks; discuss process sensitivities (voids, resin starvation) and tested lap-shear performance distributions.
technical_goals.success_metric: Empirical lap-shear datasets for at least two joining configurations under controlled cure.

technical_goals.title: Quantify barriers to production-scale sheets at aerospace quality
technical_goals.description: Enumerate throughput limits, yield loss drivers, environmental controls, and capital barriers—mapped to realistic ramp timelines.
technical_goals.success_metric: Traceable barrier list grounded in factory observations.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: Bullet narrative aligned to RFI requested information items.

technical_goals.title: Structural substantiation: static & fatigue evidence
technical_goals.description: Present coupon/element-level results for in-plane tension/compression, ILSS, and fatigue (R-ratio stated) vs baseline carbon/epoxy control panels matched on fiber areal weight.
technical_goals.success_metric: Statistically meaningful sample sizes (n≥5 per configuration per environment unless noted).

technical_goals.title: Weight reduction & cost estimates
technical_goals.description: Provide conservative weight reduction estimate for equal strength/stiffness targets and a $/lb manufacturing cost model basis (including scrap, cure cycle time, capital amortization).
technical_goals.success_metric: Explicit assumptions table; sensitivity to yield and fiber price volatility.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: Cost model appendix within page limits.

expected_outcomes.deliverable: RFI white paper (≤5 pages) addressing all six technical areas with figures
expected_outcomes.description: Structured per DARPA-SN-62 submission format; proprietary details marked per instructions.
expected_outcomes.transition_plan: If DARPA issues a follow-on program, Stratum can expand datasets under contract—RFI does not bind either party.

project_goals.fundamental_research_justification: RFI response emphasizes controlled experiments and manufacturing economics rather than unrestricted publication intent.
project_goals.revolutionary_vs_evolutionary: Positions graphene interlayers as a potential evolutionary-but-material weight/stiffness lever when manufacturing-controlled—not a replacement for primary fiber architecture without substantiation.
project_goals.competitive_landscape: Multiple vendors claim large-area graphene; differentiation is traceable structural datasets and aerospace process discipline—not marketing brochures.
project_goals.transition_and_commercialization: Primary transition path is insertion as qualified interlayer/adhesive additive into existing carbon/epoxy supply chains for UAV and regional jet tier suppliers.

export_control.categories: EAR may apply to certain manufacturing equipment and detailed process parameters; ITAR generally not applicable unless defense-specific applications are detailed.
export_control.plan: RFI response will separate commercial capabilities summary from proprietary process parameters; detailed foreign disclosure restrictions on manufacturing tours.

security_requirements.cui_categories: RFI expected unclassified; markings per respondent determination.
security_requirements.facility_requirements: Commercial facility controls; no classified spaces.

compliance_and_constraints.independent_research_and_development: Internal IRAD supports coupon-scale graphene trials not billed to government unless awarded.

prior_government_funding.relationship: Historical; unrelated to graphene sheet scale-up except processing discipline carryover.

conflicts_of_interest.organizational_conflicts: Stratum does not provide DARPA SETA/A&AS support.
conflicts_of_interest.mitigation: NDAs with partners; segregated teams for blinded replicate testing.

compliance_and_constraints.special_considerations: RFI explicitly excludes carbon nanotubes/particles and discourages modeling-only responses; Stratum's narrative is anchored to measured structural coupons and manufacturing throughput observations.
